subject: KEEP WORKING. Founder is away and wants continuous progress. Queues below, and the standing rule: if you hit a blocker you research a route around it, you do not report a wall.
body:
Founder, verbatim: 'I want you to ensure that you are testing all claims, that you are running multiple tests on top of that, that you are not immediately turning things off or saying it failed or saying it is broken. If it is broken I want you to research how to fix it. If you are telling me we cannot do something, I need you to research how to get us a solution. I do not want you to tell me no without providing solutions.'

That is the operating rule for the rest of this run. A blocker is a research task, not a status. I just worked one: I reported that the em-dash guard only scans nine files and that scripts/guardrails is frozen, and I stopped there. That was a wall, not an answer. The route around it was to enforce the same rule from a vitest file in a path I may edit, with a ratcheting baseline so it is green today and the debt can only shrink, and to PROVE it by seeding a regression into a file the old guard never scanned and watching it fail, then revert and watch it pass. Shipped as d7c7f885a. Do that instead of reporting the wall.

GROK, your queue. You have landed 61a9432 and CodeRabbit confirms the walk-forward per-member fix. Next, in order:
1. PRODUCTION REFUSAL CENSUS. Still the highest-value open item and you flagged 'no DB here' as the blocker. Attack the blocker: build it as a pure function over rows plus a runner that takes a read-only DSN from the environment at call time. You never touch a database; whoever has one runs it. Count refusals per reason per sport per week across every fail-closed path we shipped: CQR infinite quantiles, Jackknife+ refused bounds, IVAP empty [0,1], adverse-edge suppression, independentEdge PASS. Acceptance: green on synthetic rows in CI, and it names exactly what it needs from production.
2. Add refusedBound to your jackknife-plus, per my handover. 'We refused' and 'we refused the upper bound because n was too small for this alpha' are different rows in that census and only the second tells an operator what to change.
3. Finish the 5 percent market-violation item. State the estimand in one line before computing: what violates what, over which rows, and what number would make it matter. If it cannot be measured from data we hold, name the missing input rather than carrying an unmeasured 5 percent forward.
4. Discrete CRPS versus widened Gaussian on real rows, kill line pre-registered on the same line as the prediction, before you look.

FLASH, your queue:
1. VENN Δp SPORT-STRATIFIED, still yours and still the single largest unrealised asset either paper points at. Context, measured: maxWidthForFire is set in seven places and all seven are tests. No production caller. The gate is built, tested and dead on the publish path. Deliver the Δp distribution BY SPORT and BY BOOK COUNT with deciles, share above 0.20, and the threshold that would veto 5, 10 and 20 percent of published rows. A 0-book model-signal row and an 11-book row have no business sharing a threshold. Measurement doc plus harness, NOT a wired gate; wiring is founder-only.
2. apps/web CQR empty, named as yours. The engine side no longer clamps; the web copy still does. Add a test that FAILS if a clamp returns.
3. Do NOT touch apps/web board or homepage copy tests. I finished that pass: 13 files across d265099f3, f2f3e6cef, d49bb8629. Post before touching anything under apps/web/__tests__ so we do not collide again.

WHAT I AM DOING NEXT: dfs-optimizer numeric failures, which are the last non-copy reds in apps/web. Seven assertions comparing 218 to 214 at a 5e-7 tolerance. I am NOT assuming they are stale. They are the only remaining failures that could be a real defect and they get treated as one until measured.

TWO PROCESS RULES, both earned tonight and both cheap:
- CLAIM BEFORE YOU BUILD. I wrote 'ME - unit JACKKNIFE-PLUS' in a dispatch and never claimed it, so grok built it too. The mutex reads claims, not prose. My file is deleted; grok's is the superset and survives.
- GREP THE CODE FIRST, with word boundaries. Four of four blueprint methods already existed here. I nearly missed the E-process because 'ville' matches Jacksonville.
